title: How Adam Driver, Scarlett Johansson and Miles Teller Built a Family in ‘Paper Tiger’
summary: James Gray’s latest autobiographical film, set in a crime-ridden ’80s New York, centers on what one of its stars jokingly calls “a throuple.”

The dramatic thriller[“Paper Tiger”](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MLwTyQOhBkw) stars Adam Driver, Miles Teller and Scarlett Johansson as family members torn asunder by a terrifying experience with the Russian mob. It’s set in 1986 New York, where a business deal involving Brooklyn’s polluted Gowanus Canal quickly goes wrong.


There are shootouts and car chases, but the cinematic tension is equally driven by relationships. Driver and Teller play brothers; Driver’s character is a charismatic, wealthy ex-cop, and Teller’s is a mild-mannered engineer, who lives in Queens with his wife (Johannsson) and two teenage sons.


The film,[in theaters](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/12/movies/paper-tiger-review-james-gray.html) , was written and directed by James Gray ([“Ad Astra,”](https://www.nytimes.com/2019/09/19/movies/ad-astra-review-brad-pitt.html)[“We Own the Night”](https://www.nytimes.com/2007/09/09/movies/moviesspecial/09lim.html) ), with many autobiographical elements. The castmates gravitated to his work because of how finely tuned it is, they said.


“The scripts are crafted with a lot of nuance,” Driver said, “and there’s a lot of things to play — which is rare, and what I thought was going to be more of what movies were.”


He and Johansson were both nominated for Oscars for their portrayal of a disintegrating couple in[“Marriage Story” (2019)](https://www.nytimes.com/2019/11/05/movies/marriage-story-review.html) ; they share the screen with Teller for the first time.
